blindSummary: Public visibility under municipal pressure: municipal practice of a far-right party in this state/province's mining basin. Around thirty local associations accuse newly won far-right town halls of cancelling or hollowing out local Pride events while claiming to defend LGBT rights (the move is described as pinkwashing); party representatives have voted against conversion-therapy resolutions. This is a documented pattern across several communes, not one mayor's statement. The state/province combines a large student-oriented scene in its main city with conservative voting patterns in rural areas. National context from this record's sources: trans detainees in prisons are placed by the gender on their identity documents (criminal-procedure provisions), fall into a legal grey area and are punished beyond their alleged crimes — the national detention oversight body says transgender detainees are the group that "suffers the most" in detention; its 2021 Opinion covering all places of deprivation of liberty (based on ~40 referrals since 2010) finds serious violations persisting, with isolation, untrained staff and unimplemented 2016 depathologisation identified as the structural causes.
blindSourceSummaries: Investigative feature (Jan 2018) on transgender women in prisons: by law, placement follows the gender on identity documents (criminal-procedure provisions), so trans women legally marked male are held in all-male facilities — a case of three days in a men's facility near the region's largest city after transfer in 2014, shouted at and threatened by inmates; another held under notorious conditions after a 2016 protest trial; the national detention oversight body states transgender detainees are the group that "suffers the most" in prison.

National detention oversight body's Opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in all places of deprivation of liberty: serious violations persist across institutions (based on ~40 referrals since 2010 plus interviews and inspections); recommends that detained people choose the gender of their search officer and ward, no isolation because of trans identity, no dedicated trans-only wards, and ongoing hormone/medical care; extends to intersex and non-binary people; notes the 2016 depathologising law has not been translated into prison rules.

International anti-torture body interview with the national detention mechanism (May 2023) about its 2021 Opinion: trans persons in detention face constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; research found a lack of data on trans detainees' numbers and locations, almost no staff training, and no guidance implementing the 2016 law; central recommendation is that detaining authorities ask people what they require and respond; five dedicated inspection visits were carried out across regions and institution types.
blindTangential: The far-right municipal pattern documented here targets LGBTQ pride events and organisations broadly rather than gender expression specifically, but cancellations and hollowed-out permits directly reduce safe public space for gender-nonconforming visitors and residents in affected communes.
